requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 communicate through node1 (routed topology, since unconfigured)
requirements.summary: node1 eth1/eth2 assigned static IPs (10.10.12.1/24, 10.10.13.1/24); node2/node3 enp8s0 assigned persistent static IPs and cross-subnet routes via nmcli; ip_forward=1 confirmed on node1; end-to-end ping node2<->node3 through node1 succeeded before and after shaping/restarts.

requirements.requirement: Limit traffic from node2 toward node3 to 1 Mbit/s
requirements.summary: Unshaped baseline node2->node3 throughput measured at ~24 Gbit/s. A VyOS qos rate-control policy (tbf, 1Mbit) was applied on eth2 egress (node3-facing interface on node1), confirmed installed via 'show qos interface eth2' and 'tc qdisc show'. Post-config iperf3 measured node2->node3 throughput at ~0.96-1.2 Mbit/s, matching the target.

requirements.requirement: Leave traffic from node3 toward node2 unrestricted
requirements.summary: No qos policy was applied to eth1 (node2-facing interface); iperf3 from node3->node2 measured ~1.05-1.34 Gbit/s, consistent with unshaped Gigabit-class throughput, directly demonstrating the reverse direction remains unrestricted.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (32669db3...) captured; reboot acknowledged, connection dropped and recovered; post-restart boot_id (210243e0...) differs; QoS policy, eth1/eth2 IPs, ip_forward, and tbf qdisc all confirmed persisted via VyOS config.boot; end-to-end ping through node1 recovered.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node2
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (55595e92...) captured; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id (51e51ee4...) differs; static IP/route on enp8s0 confirmed intact (nmcli-persisted); iperf3 re-confirmed node2->node3 shaping still enforced (~0.97-1.4Mbit/s) after restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node3
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (4999270d...) captured; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id (318f82f3...) differs; static IP/route confirmed intact; final bidirectional iperf3 test after all three restarts confirms node2->node3 still ~0.97-1.3Mbit/s and node3->node2 unrestricted (~508Mbit-1.5Gbit/s).

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct, before/after evidence: the previously-unconfigured node2-node1-node3 routed topology was built and verified end-to-end; a VyOS tbf-based qos policy was applied to node1's node3-facing interface (eth2 egress) capping node2->node3 throughput from ~24Gbit/s baseline to ~1Mbit/s while node3->node2 remained at Gigabit-class throughput (unrestricted); and the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was completed for all three nodes with matching pre/post boot identities, acknowledged reboots, and full recovery of network configuration, IP forwarding, QoS policy, and shaping behavior (re-verified via iperf3 after each restart, including a final post-all-restarts bidirectional test).
limitations: Minor residue was left behind (iperf3 package installed on node2/node3, and /tmp/iperf_server.log and /tmp/reboot.log log files) that was not cleaned up, though it is low-risk and unrelated to security or functional correctness.

Evidence for the qos policy's directionality relies on interface-level tc qdisc/show qos output plus throughput measurements rather than an explicit packet-level trace distinguishing traffic direction, though the throughput asymmetry (1Mbit/s vs Gbit/s) strongly corroborates correct directional shaping.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map clearly to task or evidence-collection purposes and were cleaned up: temporary firewalld port 5201 openings on node2/node3 were opened and removed multiple times across test cycles (cmd-25d471985e2448d7/cmd-6f2cccbc834c42e8, cmd-15d25be48f9e47f7/cmd-4f911062031c4286, cmd-c5ec8791aacd41d4/cmd-683484baa58e4d18, cmd-5160c34ee1844513/cmd-1878f72d380d4151 finally closed via cmd-a37aa57ca606488b and cmd-262ac11b913b4c28); iperf3 server background processes were pkill'd after each test. One bounded, low-risk troubleshooting mutation occurred: manual 'ip addr add' on node2/node3 enp8s0 (cmd-011ab98da07642d4, cmd-5d237f10388841d3) was later superseded by the persistent nmcli configuration (cmd-8bb2d725edd946fa, cmd-8443290f2c4547a5), leaving no residue in final state. Minor unrestored residue: iperf3 package remains installed on node2/node3 (used only for bandwidth verification, not part of the task) and /tmp/iperf_server.log plus /tmp/reboot.log were left on node2/node3 per the after-executor temporary-files diff. These are low-impact, non-security-relevant leftovers rather than broad or destructive changes.
